issues.description: Docs complect 'preview as data contract' with 'preview as renderer config' via meta
issues.detail: The meta parameter is documented as both general metadata (versions, timestamps) and renderer control (Mermaid layout, syntax language). One field, two unrelated concerns — classic complecting. A preview value should be a value; renderer hints belong in a separate field or a separate type. Docs should name this split, not normalize the conflation.

issues.description: Closure pattern for 'data context' hides time/identity instead of making them explicit
issues.detail: The make_preview_fn closure example captures sample_data at pipeline-construction time and calls it 'data context'. That's place-oriented: the value is frozen at one moment, but the preview is invoked later and looks live. Docs should state plainly when the preview snapshot was taken, or recommend passing a function that reads the current value.

issues.description: preview_fn has no access to node inputs/outputs — essential question dodged
issues.detail: Docs admit 'Preview functions don't have access to node inputs or outputs directly' and route users to closures or ad-hoc dataset access. That is the essential question: what value is being previewed, of what identity, at what time? The design pushes that onto every user. Docs should name this as a known limitation, not present a workaround as the pattern.

issues.description: Seven preview subclasses where one tagged value would do
issues.detail: JsonPreview, TablePreview, PlotlyPreview, MermaidPreview, ImagePreview, TextPreview, CustomPreview are seven types whose only real difference is a renderer tag and a content shape. A single Preview value with kind and content fields would be simpler. The docs amplify the type-per-renderer pattern; worth a note that CustomPreview already proves the general case.

issues.description: preview.to_dict() shown without explaining what the value actually is
issues.detail: The basic example calls preview.to_dict() with the comment 'Serialise for APIs/frontends' but never says what the canonical value is — the object or the dict. If the preview is just data, the object wrapper is incidental complexity. Docs should state which form is the value of record and why both exist.

issues.description: Experimental warning is real but buried; no guidance on stability of preview payload shape
issues.detail: The experimental warning at the top is correct, but the doc then specifies meta keys, renderer_key semantics, and Mermaid config schemas as if stable. Readers will build against these. State explicitly which surfaces are likely to move (subclass set, meta schema, renderer_key contract) so users don't complect their code with a moving target.

review.summary: The docs do a competent job of teaching the surface of preview_fn, but they normalize several complected design choices instead of naming them. The meta field carries both metadata-about-the-value and renderer-configuration; the closure pattern silently freezes a sample at construction time while looking live; the admission that previews can't see node inputs or outputs is buried inside a 'best practice.' Seven preview subclasses where one tagged value would suffice, and a to_dict() call shown without clarifying which form is the value of record. None of this is a P0 — it is documentation of an experimental feature — but the docs should name the complecting they are teaching users to live with, and label the experimental surface area more sharply so readers know what is load-bearing.
